lem-local-lipschitz-class-empirical-proc:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID with law $P$, and let
$f_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable for $t$ in a neighbourhood of
$0\in\mathbb R^d$. Assume $f_0=0$ and that on one $P$-full set
$$|f_t(x)-f_s(x)|\le M(x)\|t-s\|_2$$
for all such $s,t$, where $M\ge0$ is measurable and $P M^2<\infty$. For
$P_nf=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf(X_i)$, both displayed sample-path suprema are
measurable and
there is a finite constant $C_d$, depending only on $d$, such that for every
radius $r$ whose closed ball is in the parameter neighbourhood,
$$E\sup_{\|t\|_2\le r}|\sqrt n(P_n-P)f_t|\le C_d r(PM^2)^{1/2}.$$
Moreover, for $0<\varepsilon\le r$,
$$E\sup_{\substack{\|s\|_2,\|t\|_2\le r\\\|t-s\|_2\le\varepsilon}}|\sqrt n(P_n-P)(f_t-f_s)|\le C_d\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(e r/\varepsilon)}(PM^2)^{1/2}.$$
thm-lan-implies-total-variation-bvm:
## Statement

Assume AC. For each $n$, let $X^{(n)}$ have law $P_{0,n}$ on a measurable
space, and let $\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open, $d\ge1$. Suppose a
supplied sigma-finite measure $\mu_n$ dominates $P_{0,n}$ and the model laws
$P_{n,\theta}$, and suppose jointly measurable finite-valued densities
$p_{0,n}$ and $p_{n,\theta}$ are supplied. Fix an interior point
$\theta^*\in\Theta$ with $p_{n,\theta^*}(X^{(n)})>0$
$P_{0,n}$-almost surely. Let the prior be a proper Lebesgue density $\pi$
continuous and strictly positive on a neighbourhood of $\theta^*$, and assume
the displayed likelihood integral is finite and positive almost surely so it
defines the posterior
$$\Pi_n(A\mid X^{(n)})=\frac{\int_Ap_{n,\theta}(X^{(n)})\pi(\theta)\,d\theta}{\int_\Theta p_{n,\theta}(X^{(n)})\pi(\theta)\,d\theta}.$$
For $\delta_n>0$ with $\delta_n\to0$, write
$$\ell_n(\theta)=\log\frac{p_{n,\theta}(X^{(n)})}{p_{n,\theta^*}(X^{(n)})}.$$
Assume $V$ is a fixed symmetric positive-definite $d\times d$ matrix,
$\Delta_n=O_{P_{0,n}}(1)$, and for every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^d$,
$$\sup_{h\in K}\left|\ell_n(\theta^*+\delta_nh)-h^T\Delta_n+\tfrac12h^TVh\right|=o_{P_{0,n}}(1).$$
Also assume that for every deterministic sequence $M_n\to\infty$,
$$\Pi_n\!\left(\|\theta-\theta^*\|_2>\delta_nM_n\mid X^{(n)}\right)=o_{P_{0,n}}(1).$$
Then the posterior law of $H_n=\delta_n^{-1}(\theta-\theta^*)$ satisfies
$$\left\|\Pi_n(H_n\in\cdot\mid X^{(n)})-N_d(V^{-1}\Delta_n,V^{-1})\right\|_{\rm TV}=o_{P_{0,n}}(1),$$
where $\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|$ over measurable sets. The
LAN condition concerns likelihood-density ratios on the $P_{0,n}$-full set
where the denominator is positive; it does not assert a Radon–Nikodym
derivative for the entire local model law.
cor-qmd-ac-component-lan-to-bvm:
## Statement

Assume AC and a common-dominator iid model with supplied densities that is
QMD at an interior $\theta^*$, with $P_0=P_{\theta^*}$. Put
$p_0=p_{\theta^*}$, $S=\{p_0>0\}$, and
$\alpha(u)=P_{\theta^*+u}(S^c)$. On $S$, the normalized absolutely
continuous component has $P_0$-density
$$q_u(x)=\frac{p_{\theta^*+u}(x)}{(1-\alpha(u))p_0(x)}.$$
For $u=h/\sqrt n$, suppose that for every compact $H\subset\mathbb R^d$,
the proxy log likelihood satisfies
$$\sup_{h\in H}\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\log q_{h/\sqrt n}(X_i)-h^T\Delta_n+\tfrac12h^TVh\right|=o_{P_0}(1),$$
with $\Delta_n=O_{P_0}(1)$ and $V\succ0$. Assume also the proper prior,
positive finite posterior evidence, and parameter-rate contraction hypotheses
of [[thm-lan-implies-total-variation-bvm]]. Then its total-variation BvM
conclusion holds for the actual posterior. The compact-uniform proxy-LAN
condition is an additional hypothesis: [[thm-qmd-implies-lan-for-iid]]
asserts LAN only along each fixed convergent local sequence. No full
likelihood ratio for the whole local alternative is asserted.
thm-misspecified-iid-lan-under-kv-smooth:
## Statement

Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID from $P_0$ on a measurable space, and let
$\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open, $d\ge1$. Suppose a sigma-finite measure
$\mu$ and jointly measurable finite-valued densities $p_0,p_\theta$ are
supplied, with $P_0(dx)=p_0(x)\mu(dx)$, $P_\theta(dx)=p_\theta(x)\mu(dx)$,
and $p_{\theta^*}>0$ $P_0$-almost surely. Define the directional contrast
$$K(\theta)=E_0\log\frac{p_0(X)}{p_\theta(X)}.$$
Assume $K$ is finite near an interior point $\theta^*$, $\theta^*$ is a
finite minimizer of $K$, and, for $t\to0$,
$$E_0\log\frac{p_{\theta^*}(X)}{p_{\theta^*+t}(X)}=\tfrac12t^TVt+o(\|t\|_2^2)$$
for a fixed symmetric positive-definite matrix $V$. Assume also that a
measurable random vector $s(X)\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies
$$\frac{\log p_{\theta^*+t}(X)-\log p_{\theta^*}(X)-t^Ts(X)}{\|t\|_2}\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0$-probability as $t\to0$ through nonzero vectors, and that on a
neighbourhood $U$ of $\theta^*$ there is a common $P_0$-almost-sure bound
$$\left|\log\frac{p_{\theta_1}(X)}{p_{\theta_2}(X)}\right|\le M(X)\|\theta_1-\theta_2\|_2\qquad(\theta_1,\theta_2\in U),$$
where $M\ge0$ and $E_0M^2<\infty$. Then $E_0s=0$ and
$I=E_0[ss^T]$ is finite. With $S_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^ns(X_i)$ and
$\Delta_n=V^{-1}S_n$, for every compact $H\subset\mathbb R^d$,
$$\sup_{h\in H}\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\log\frac{p_{\theta^*+h/\sqrt n}(X_i)}{p_{\theta^*}(X_i)}-h^TS_n+\tfrac12h^TVh\right|=o_{P_0}(1).$$
In particular $\Delta_n=O_{P_0}(1)$. No equality between $I$ and $V$ is
assumed; under misspecification they generally differ.
cor-misspecified-iid-bvm-under-kv-regula:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-misspecified-iid-lan-under-kv-smoothness]] at
$\theta^*$, and assume AC. Let a proper prior have a Lebesgue density
continuous and strictly positive near $\theta^*$, and suppose the posterior
has finite positive evidence almost surely and contracts in Euclidean
parameter norm outside $n^{-1/2}M_n$ for every deterministic $M_n\to\infty$.
Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n(\theta-\theta^*)$ is
$$o_{P_0}(1)\text{ in total variation from }N_d(V^{-1}S_n,V^{-1}),\qquad S_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^ns(X_i).$$
The parameter-rate contraction is an explicit premise. Ordinary consistency
at a KL projection alone does not discharge it.
thm-misspecified-mle-sandwich-expansion:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-misspecified-iid-lan-under-kv-smoothness]]
and AC. Let $\widehat\theta_n$ be a measurable estimator such that
$\widehat\theta_n\to\theta^*$ in $P_0$-probability and
$$P_n\log p_{\widehat\theta_n}\ge \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}P_n\log p_\theta-o_{P_0}(n^{-1}),$$
where the empirical supremum is finite and measurable and the approximation remainder is measurable. Set $P_nf=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf(X_i)$. Then, with
$I=E_0[ss^T]$ and $S_n=n^{-1/2}\sum_i s(X_i)$,
$$\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta^*)=V^{-1}S_n+o_{P_0}(1)\ \Rightarrow\ N_d(0,V^{-1}IV^{-1}).$$
Thus the MLE sampling covariance is the sandwich matrix $V^{-1}IV^{-1}$,
whereas the BvM posterior covariance is $V^{-1}$. If the posterior also
satisfies the contraction premise of
[[thm-lan-implies-total-variation-bvm]], then its Gaussian limit may be
recentered at $\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta^*)$ in total variation. The
consistency and approximate-maximization hypotheses are separate assumptions;
this theorem proves neither MLE consistency nor existence of an MLE.
